title: A map of a language region and a table of voting results: devolution and its causes

readings.title: Source 1: Speakers of the Dorvan language in Country A
Source 2: A vote on more self-rule for the south
readings.html:
Results by province of a vote, held in five provinces, on giving the south its own elected assembly (invented data for practice)
ProvinceYesNoTurnout
South Coast71%29%52%
Southern Forest64%36%58%
Western Uplands41%59%60%
Central Valley22%78%63%
Capital Region15%85%70%

Invented data for practice.

parts.label: A
parts.demand: Give the information asked for: a word or short phrase can earn the point, with no reasons needed.
parts.prompt: Identify the scale of analysis of the data shown in Source 1.

rubric.point: Names the local (subnational or provincial) scale.

parts.sample: The scale of analysis is local (subnational), because the data are given for each province of Country A.

parts.label: B
parts.demand: Give the relevant characteristics: what it is like, where and how much. A name alone earns nothing.
parts.prompt: Describe the pattern of Dorvan speakers shown in Source 1.

rubric.point: Says where Dorvan speakers are concentrated and where they are few, naming provinces or directions.
accept: concentrated in the south (Southern Forest, South Coast)
few in the Capital Region, north and east

parts.sample: Dorvan speakers are concentrated in the south: they are 70% or more of the people in the Southern Forest and South Coast, and their share falls to under 10% in the Capital Region and the north and east.

parts.label: C
parts.demand: Say how or why, with every link of the chain: a cause, then because or so, then its effect, tied to the place or data asked about.
parts.prompt: Explain how language can act as a centrifugal force in Country A.

rubric.point: Links the language difference to division (feeling left out, separate identity) that pulls the south away.
accept: a separate language builds a separate identity, so the south pulls away
schools or government in another language make southerners feel left out

parts.sample: Because most people in the south speak Dorvan while the capital and the north speak another language, southerners may feel that national schools and government do not serve them, so the language difference pulls the south away from the rest of the state.

parts.label: D
parts.demand: Give the relevant characteristics: what it is like, where and how much. A name alone earns nothing.
parts.prompt: Using both sources, describe the relationship between the share of Dorvan speakers and the Yes vote.

rubric.point: Describes a positive relationship with values from both sources.
accept: more Dorvan speakers, higher Yes vote
South Coast 70% or more Dorvan and 71% Yes; Capital Region under 10% and 15% Yes

parts.sample: Provinces with more Dorvan speakers voted Yes more strongly: the South Coast and Southern Forest, where 70% or more speak Dorvan, voted 71% and 64% Yes, while the Capital Region, under 10% Dorvan, voted only 15% Yes.

parts.label: E
parts.demand: Say how or why, with every link of the chain: a cause, then because or so, then its effect, tied to the place or data asked about.
parts.prompt: Explain one factor other than language that could push the south toward devolution.

rubric.point: Names a non-language factor (economic, physical division, unequal services) and links it to demands for self-rule.
accept: economic: the south feels it pays more taxes than it gets back, so it wants control of its money
physical division: distance from the capital makes the south feel ignored
uneven services or jobs, so resentment grows

parts.sample: An economic factor: if people in the south feel that roads, jobs and spending go to the Capital Region first, resentment grows, so southerners demand more control over their own money and decisions.

parts.label: F
parts.demand: Say how or why, with every link of the chain: a cause, then because or so, then its effect, tied to the place or data asked about.
parts.prompt: Explain how Country A's government could reduce the pressure for devolution.

rubric.point: Names a policy and links it to less pressure (for example, regional powers or fairer spending leads to less reason to leave).
accept: give the south an assembly or autonomy, so it governs what matters most
protect Dorvan in schools, so speakers feel included
spend more fairly in the south, so resentment falls

parts.sample: The government could give the south an elected assembly with control over its schools and language, as Spain did for its autonomous communities, so Dorvan speakers would govern the matters they care about most and have less reason to seek independence.

parts.label: G
parts.demand: State the degree first (to a high, moderate or low degree), then explain why with evidence.
parts.prompt: Explain the degree to which the results in Source 2 show that the south wants to become an independent state.

rubric.point: States a degree, then explains a limit of the data (the vote was about self-rule, not independence; turnout; provinces vary).
accept: to a limited degree: the vote was for more self-rule, not independence
turnout in the South Coast was only 52%, so many views are unknown

parts.sample: To a limited degree: the south voted Yes, but the vote was about an assembly for more self-rule, not independence, and turnout in the South Coast was only 52%, so the results cannot show what most southerners want about leaving.
